pr_title: kubelet: assign Node as an owner for the ResourceSlice
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

It sets a kubelet node as an owner for the ResourceSlice. This ensures that NodeSlice objects will be garbage collected if node object is removed.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #123692
Fixes #123691

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: DRA: kubelet: avoid API permission error log entries
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

When kubelet starts and begins watching NodeResourceSlice objects with an informer, it initially logs errors like:
```
 E0226 13:41:19.880621  126334 reflector.go:150] k8s.io/client-go@v0.0.0/tools/cache/reflector.go:232: Failed to watch *v1alpha2.NodeResourceSlice: failed to list *v1alpha2.NodeResourceSlice: noderesourceslices.resource.k8s.io is forbidden: User "system:anonymous" cannot list resource "noderesourceslices" in API group "resource.k8s.io" at the cluster scope
 ```
 
 This seems to be caused by the informer being started at a time when the kubelet REST client doesn't have the final credentials yet. The errors are harmless and can be ignored because eventually the List call succeeds.

Ideas for solving this:
- change when the registration handler is called or
- wait in the `pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/noderesources.go` code until List succeeds without logging errors, then start the informer
 

### Why is this needed?

Error logs are confusing.

/sig node
/triage accepted
/priority important-longterm
/lifecycle frozen
/assign
comments:
This problem is not limited to the DRA manager. There are other, similar errors in the kubelet log and (according to @klueska) in the scheduler log (or was it the controller?).

Might be worth looking for a more general solution.

review_comments:
@pohly I failed to figure out how to correctly do this. Can you help?
Another question: Is it possible to check that the length of the `OwnerReferences` is always 1 using gstruct API?

You need to do the same as I did below in `matchSlice`: create a matcher that verifies that the `OwnerReferences` slice matches exactly one element.

It's debatable whether that element should be described with a `gomega.Equal(metav1.OwnerReference{...})` or another `gomega.MatchAllFields` - both works. But let's not use `gstruct.MatchFields(gstruct.IgnoreExtras`, that is not precise enough.

Here's a patch that makes your branch pass for me. Note that setting `Controller` was missing in your code. Without it, the reference is merely informative and doesn't trigger garbage collection (if I remember correctly - documentation of that field is poor).

```patch
diff --git a/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/noderesources.go b/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/noderesources.go
index 0a34c5ee898..58936013c04 100644
--- a/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/noderesources.go
+++ b/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/noderesources.go
@@ -40,6 +40,7 @@ import (
 	"k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue"
 	"k8s.io/klog/v2"
 	drapb "k8s.io/kubelet/pkg/apis/dra/v1alpha3"
+	"k8s.io/utils/ptr"
 )
 
 const (
@@ -469,6 +470,7 @@ func (c *nodeResourcesController) sync(ctx context.Context, driverName string) e
 						Kind:       v1.SchemeGroupVersion.WithKind("Node").Kind,
 						Name:       node.Name,
 						UID:        node.UID,
+						Controller: ptr.To(true),
 					},
 				},
 			},
diff --git a/test/e2e/dra/dra.go b/test/e2e/dra/dra.go
index 252d0e20300..2a9e6d89ccb 100644
--- a/test/e2e/dra/dra.go
+++ b/test/e2e/dra/dra.go
@@ -905,16 +905,22 @@ var _ = framework.SIGDescribe("node")("DRA", feature.DynamicResourceAllocation,
 				resourceClient := f.ClientSet.ResourceV1alpha2().ResourceSlices()
 				var expectedObjects []any
 				for _, nodeName := range nodes.NodeNames {
+					node, err := f.ClientSet.CoreV1().Nodes().Get(ctx, nodeName, metav1.GetOptions{})
+					framework.ExpectNoError(err, "get node")
 					expectedObjects = append(expectedObjects,
 						gstruct.MatchAllFields(gstruct.Fields{
 							"TypeMeta": gstruct.Ignore(),
 							"ObjectMeta": gstruct.MatchFields(gstruct.IgnoreExtras, gstruct.Fields{
-								"OwnerReferences": gstruct.MatchElements(func(element interface{}) string { return element.(metav1.OwnerReference).Kind }, gstruct.IgnoreExtras, gstruct.Elements{
-									"OwnerReference": gstruct.MatchFields(gstruct.IgnoreExtras, gstruct.Fields{
-										"kind": gomega.Equal("Node"),
-										"name": gomega.Equal(nodeName),
+								"OwnerReferences": gomega.ContainElements(
+									gstruct.MatchAllFields(gstruct.Fields{
+										"APIVersion":         gomega.Equal("v1"),
+										"Kind":               gomega.Equal("Node"),
+										"Name":               gomega.Equal(nodeName),
+										"UID":                gomega.Equal(node.UID),
+										"Controller":         gomega.Equal(ptr.To(true)),
+										"BlockOwnerDeletion": gomega.BeNil(),
 									}),
-								}),
+								),
 							}),
 							"NodeName":   gomega.Equal(nodeName),
 							"DriverName": gomega.Equal(driver.Name),
```

Could it be that this node changes later? I don't know, therefore I am wary of making the assumption that it doesn't.

Perhaps better call this whenever an object needs to be updated or created? It's reading from a local cache, so it's not that expensive.

I don't think we need to re-sync when the node object changes. The only way how this can cause the UID to change is when the old node object gets removed. Unless users work really hard to breaks us, all old slices will get removed, which triggers syncing.

Thank you for the review and suggestions!

I agree that node name or UID are unlikely to change. However, `getNode` will always get the latest available node object version from the cache. At least I hope it will. Alternatively we can just store node name and UID in the `nodeResourcesController struct`. What would you suggest?
I suggest to call `getNode` anew in `sync`
it's already called there, so I'll leave the code as it is.

I missed that because this code here remained.

Can you simplify it (no need for separate variables, no need for `node`) and add a comment why we have this loop here?

> We're using node object a bit below these lines, so we need it:

Ah, right.

BTW, if you cannot reply to a comment in GitHub, then you need to go to the thread where that comment was added to reply.
ok, will do. Thanks for the explanations :)

@pohly This might also fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123691
At least I don't see `resourceslices.resource.k8s.io is forbidden` in the kubelet logs in my environment.
Yes. We now block for the node informer to populate its cache, which implies that the `kubeClient` is usable.
Please add a comment about why we get the node anew each time, otherwise someone might get the idea later that this should be optimized.
Than you for the review. Added.
